NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  Pursuant to the Governor's Executive Order N-29-20, City Council Members will be participating via
  teleconference.

  - City Council meetings are recorded and live-streamed on the City’s website at www.rhe.city and
  available for viewing thereafter, and televised on Cox 33 and Frontier FiOS 38 on Wednesday and Friday
  following the meeting.

  - Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1-669-900-6833) from any phone,
  Meeting ID: 828 4087 7375, Meeting Password: 066081. (Please note you will not have the ability to
  speak using the call-in option from a phone line.)

  - Public correspondence may be emailed to the City Clerk at laurenp@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails
  received before 5:00 p.m. the night of the Council meeting will be forwarded to the City Council for their
  consideration and included as part of the record.

  - Members of the public may comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes &
  Videos” page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there
  will be an “eComment” button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to
  the City’s SpeakUp page. After you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda.
  These comments can be seen by the public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the
  record.

  - Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
  Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store),
  by entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 828 4087 7375, Meeting Password: 066081. Members
  of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the following
  process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at the
  lower portion of your screen. The City Clerk will send you a chat message to identify which item on the
  agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city.

MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  OCTOBER 27, 2020

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order
by MAYOR SCHMITZ at 7:01 p.m. via teleconference, pursuant to the Governor’s Executive
Order N-29-20.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit
  Community Services Supervisor Cynthia Morquecho
  Administrative Analyst Jessica Slawson

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

None.

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority
consent of the City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good
cause is shown by a member prior to the roll call vote. (Items removed for individual
consideration will be voted on separately.)

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  MITCHELL, TO APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 6A-G AS FOLLOWS BY
  THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS BY TITLE ONLY

  APPROVED.

B.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS OF OCTOBER 2020

  APPROVED WARRANTS 63267 THROUGH 63315 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $185,886.08 AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 100320 THROUGH
  100520; 63151 VOID; IN THE AMOUNT OF $104,202.73 FOR A GRAND
  TOTAL AMOUNT OF $290,088.81 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

C.  SCHEDULE OF INVESTMENTS REPORT OF SEPTEMBER 2020

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

D.  REVENUE AND EXPENDITURE REPORT OF SEPTEMBER 2020

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
OCTOBER 27, 2020
 E.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF OCTOBER 13, 2020 SPECIAL JOINT MEETING

  REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

F.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF OCTOBER 13, 2020

  REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

G.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF OCTOBER 19, 2020

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

Seforah Teferi from Peninsula High School provided information about a school organization
called Kick-ASH that will be holding a virtual, anti-vaping, Town Hall meeting via zoom on
October 29 at 6:00 p.m.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

NONE.

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ACTION ITEM FROM MEETING OF
  OCTOBER 19, 2020: REVISED CONCEPTUAL DESIGN FOR GEORGE F CANYON
  NATURE CENTER

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL inquired about the difference between the proposed cost of
the original design and the proposed cost of the current design, noting the reduction of $1
million. She stated that she agrees more public outreach is a good idea to allow the public to
review the new plan. She also noted residents’ concerns regarding the exit off of Hitching Post
Drive.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF stated that she would like the recommended community meeting
to have a public-forum format so that it is inviting for the public to join and participate.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN agreed with COUNCIL MEMBERS MITCHELL AND HUFF.
He also reiterated that this project has been considered and discussed for over two years with
many opportunities for public input.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN highlighted that the new proposed design is significantly
less money while larger and more functional. He also noted it will be a shared facility between
the Conservancy and the City. Lastly, he expressed concern regarding the lack of parking and
overflow parking.

MAYOR SCHMITZ echoed her fellow Council Members’ thoughts.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  DIRECT STAFF TO SCHEDULE A COMMUNITY MEETING FOR CONTINUED
  PUBLIC ENGAGEMENT WITH CITY APPOINTED AND ELECTED OFFICIALS
  OF THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION, PLANNING COMMISSION
  AND CITY COUNCIL.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
OCTOBER 27, 2020
   AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

B.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ACTION ITEM FROM MEETING OF
  OCTOBER 19, 2020: BUTCHER PARK UPDATE

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL liked the proposed design including the walkway and natural
playground concept. Assistant City Manager Davis explained the wide range of trash
receptacles being considered for the park, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL’s
question regarding the proposed cost of these receptacles.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF stated that she’s received feedback from residents who are
supportive and eager to move forward with this project and noted that Quimby funds can be
used. She stated that she would like to see less of the playground timber and more
landscaping, foliage and benches.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN stated that he has no issues with the park design, agrees
with moving forward and also agrees more benches would be nice. He also stated that the
proposed walkway could lead to the horse trail behind the park.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN stated that he is impressed with the concept, and suggested
an official name be selected for the park. He also recommended that the “below the line” items
listed on the cost sheet within the staff report should be included above the line in the total cost.
Assistant City Manager Davis explained that the Park and Activities Commission has come up
with several names, and that staff will revisit naming the park with the Commission. She also
agreed that the “below the line” items be included above the line in the total cost.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF received feedback from residents who expressed interest in
possibly donating benches. Some members of the Montecillo neighborhood suggested the
name Casaba Park in honor of the new street name.

COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL emphasized COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN’s point that
the walkway could lead to a trail, expressing the importance of connections and public access
in order to be able to walk to the park from various neighborhoods.

MAYOR SCHMITZ echoed COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL’s points, and expressed her
excitement for this project.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  MITCHELL, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE THE 2018 APPROVED CONCEPTUAL DESIGN AND
  ASSOCIATED BUDGET FOR” BUTCHER PARK” AND DIRECT STAFF TO
  RETURN WITH A PROPOSAL FOR PREPARATION OF PLANS AND
  SPECIFICATIONS FOR A PARK DEVELOPMENT PROJECT AT THE
  NORTHEAST CORNER OF PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH AND PALOS
  VERDES DRIVE EAST TEMPORARILY REFERRED TO AS “BUTCHER
  PARK” TO BE FUNDED WITH CITY PARK FACILITIES FEES AND
  PRIORITIZE THE PROJECT ACCORDINGLY.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

9.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  RESOLUTION NO. 2469 - ADOPTION OF 2020 MULTI-JURISDICTIONAL HAZARD
  MITIGATION PLAN

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
OCTOBER 27, 2020
 Administrative Analyst Slawson provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

All Council Members commended Administrative Analyst Slawson for her hard work
completing this plan for the City.

Administrative Analyst Slawson confirmed this plan will be available to the public on the City’s
website, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF confirmed that the wildfire mitigation portion of the plan would be
in coordination with Los Angeles County Fire Department.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN highlighted that staff has been working on this plan with the
City of Rancho Palos Verdes for nearly two years.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  ADOPT RESOLUTION NO 2469 APPROVING  THE  2020  MULTI-
  JURISDICTIONAL HAZARD MITIGATION PLAN.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

B.  CARES ACT SMALL BUSINESS/NON-PROFIT ASSISTANCE GRANT PROPOSAL

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Assistant City Manager Davis explained how the City has utilized the remaining $40,000 of the
total $99,000 for City operations and facilities, which was not included in the grant program, in
response to COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL. COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL noted the short
application period, and emphasized the importance of public outreach to get the word out to
the community.

Assistant City Manager Davis explained that local governments are able to spend more broadly
under the CARES Act than the businesses applying for this grant money, in response to
COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF.

Assistant City Manager Davis explained how businesses would be able to qualify for rent
assistance under this grant program, in response to MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN.

MAYOR SCHMITZ stated that the $2,500 will have a big impact on many struggling
businesses, and thanked staff for working on this grant opportunity in order to assist the
businesses in the community.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
Written late correspondence was received by Eileen Hupp on behalf of the Palos Verdes
Peninsula Chamber of Commerce, in support of the grant program.

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  ZERUNYAN, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  APPROVE THE SMALL BUSINESS AND NON-PROFIT ASSISTANCE GRANT
  REIMBURSEMENT PROGRAM AS OUTLINED TO ALLOCATE $50,000
  CARES ACT FUNDS TOWARD SMALL BUSINESSES AND $10,000 OF
  CARES ACT FUNDS TOWARD NON-PROFIT ORGANIZATIONS FOR A
  TOTAL AMOUNT OF $60,000.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
OCTOBER 27, 2020
   AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

C.  UPDATE ON LOS ANGELES COUNTY SAFER AT HOME ORDER AND STATUS OF
  CITY EVENTS (VERBAL REPORT)

City Manager Grammer provided an update on the Los Angeles County Health Officer Order,
reporting that LA County remains in Tier 1 of the State’s 4-Tier reopening plan, although the
number of cases on the Peninsula remain stable. The latest Health Officer Order allows for
some outdoor activities including batting cages, miniature golf and go-cart racing to reopen.
The lasted Order also increases the percentage of students with special or high-needs that can
be on campus at one time. Schools can also now apply for a waiver to reopen kindergarten
through second grade classes for inside instruction, in which PVPUSD has applied.

Community Services Supervisor Morquecho provided the following updates regarding
upcoming City Events:
  • October 30 will be the second drive-in movie night featuring “The Nightmare Before
  Christmas” at Ernie Howlett Park.
  • Registration opens Friday October 30 for the Holiday House Decorating Contest, which
  will be judged the week of December 7.
  • The Mayor’s Breakfast Ride will take place in November, involving a trail riding
  experience that highlights certain equestrian points of interest within the City and a video
  featuring the Mayor at each location.
  • The drive-through Parade of Lights will be held on December 5 at Ernie Howlett Park
  involving a collection of lit up light displays.
  • December 19 will be the third drive-in movie night at Ernie Howlett Park featuring the
  movie “Elf”.

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

NONE.

11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL reported on the upcoming November 4 California Air
Resources Board (CARB) joint meeting with the California Transportation Commission. She
also reported that the South Coast Air Quality Management District is having its 6th annual
Environmental Justice Conference on Wednesday, October 28.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF reported on the South Bay Cities Council of Governments
(SBCCOG) Legislative Breakfast that was held on October 16, as well as a SBCCOG Board
meeting on October 22 where she was elected to the Southern California Association of
Governments’ (SCAG) Energy and Environment Committee. She also reported that at the
November 19 SBCCOG meeting, COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL will be honored as past
president on her upcoming retirement.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN reported on the reconstitution of a SCAG subcommittee
to review the State’s recent housing legislation and the legal aspects of the process. He also
reported that California Contract Cities Association (CCCA) is working on various
collaborations for suggestions on housing policies.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN reported that the Clean Power Alliance was awarded the
Green Leadership Award by the Environmental Protection Agency for being the largest
provider of 100% clean energy in the country.

MAYOR SCHMITZ reported on the monthly Peninsula Mayors meeting, where recent
suicides among local students was discussed. She also reported that a joint meeting will be
held in the near future with the cities on the Peninsula and Southern California Edison.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS

A.  RECOMMENDATION FROM HOLIDAY PARADE SUBCOMMITTEE

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
OCTOBER 27, 2020
 Community Services Supervisor Morquecho provided a staff report (as per the agenda
material).

COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL agreed that two nights for this event would be ideal, and
expressed concern about traffic impacts, suggesting traffic control for the nights of the event.

Community Services Supervisor Morquecho explained that it would be a drive-through only
event, no walking in order to maintain safety protocols, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER
HUFF. Community Services Supervisor Morquecho noted the sponsorship goals for this
event which the City hopes will cover most of the costs.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN stated that this is a great opportunity to bring joy to the
community.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN explained the decision to have community partners involved
in the displays in addition to professionals, and echoed COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN’s
sentiments. He also noted that some sponsors may not be available or interested in
participating in two nights.

MAYOR SCHMITZ thanked the Holiday Parade subcommittee members and staff for their
efforts in putting this concept together in a safe and festive way for the community.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE CHANGES TO THE PENINSULA HOLIDAY PARADE OF LIGHTS
  TO BE HELD AS A DRIVE-THROUGH EVENT AT ERNIE HOWLETT PARK,
  ALLOWING FOR A SECOND NIGHT TO BE HELD IF THERE IS INTEREST
  FROM SPONSORS AND COMMUNITY PARTNERS, WITH A BUDGET NOT
  TO EXCEED $25,000 FOR ONE NIGHT OR $35,000 FOR TWO NIGHTS.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

13.  CLOSED SESSION

A.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL - ANTICIPATED LITIGATION
  Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(4)
  Initiation of litigation: one potential case

  NO REPORTABLE ACTION.

14.  ADJOURNMENT

At 8:45 P.M. MAYOR SCHMITZ adjourned the City Council meeting in honor of the Los
Angeles Dodgers World Series victory. The meeting was adjourned to the next regular City
Council meeting on Tuesday, November 10, 2020 at 7:00 P.M. for the purpose of a Regular
meeting.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Lauren Pettit  Velveth Schmitz
City Clerk  Mayor

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
OCTOBER 27, 2020
